minutes.headline: Board ratified the Green Communities grant, accepted three donated conservation parcels, and opened the town meeting warrant.
minutes.summary: The Select Board recognized two men for a rescue at a house fire. It heard the Green Communities task force's first-round grant plan and endorsed land valuation criteria from the open space committee and Conservation Commission. It accepted three donated parcels, heard a discouraging update on Eagle Heights senior housing financing, and opened the annual town meeting warrant. It also discussed land use coordination, broadband, and the town manager's second-quarter financial report.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to ratify the chair's signing and submission of the Green Communities grant application, whose first round asks nothing from the town.
The board accepted the donation of three parcels of land, with back taxes to be abated and the oldest parcel needing state approval.
The board approved open space land valuation criteria and endorsed the Conservation Commission's criteria for valuing land.
The board opened the annual town meeting warrant on February 4th and set it to close at 4 pm on March 24th.
The Eagle Heights senior housing agreement has expired and will not be extended until financing is clearer.

why_it_matters: The grant work and land donations affect which energy upgrades the town pays for and which land it takes on, and the warrant now open is where residents' town meeting articles are set.
The stalled Eagle Heights financing leaves the future of that senior housing project unsettled, and a projected veterans benefits deficit would be covered this year by health insurance savings.
watch_next: The building reuse committee's future charge is to be discussed at next week's board meeting.
The warrant closes at 4 pm on March 24th, and the board will seek a meeting with the planning board and land use boards.
